# 02 Resolve a parsed core sequence document into a validated SequenceModel

## Outcome

`buildGraphModel(document)` dispatches on `document.kind` to `buildFlowchartModel` (existing
logic, extracted verbatim, zero behavior change) or `buildSequenceModel` (new).
`buildSequenceModel` assigns stable message ids, enforces the explicit-reference rule (a message
or `destroy` referencing an undeclared participant is an error diagnostic), and resolves each
participant's lifeline extent for the core subset (no blocks/create/box yet — those extend this
same module in tickets 07/12).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pnpm --filter @siren/core test` still passes with zero changes to existing flowchart
  graph-model test files.
- [ ] `buildGraphModel` on a hand-built `kind: "sequence"` document dispatches to
  `buildSequenceModel` and returns `kind: "sequence"` on the resulting `GraphModelResult`'s
  `graph`/`model`.
- [ ] Two messages between the same declared pair get ids `A-B` and `A-B#2`, matching flowchart's
  existing edge-id convention.
- [ ] A message referencing a participant id never declared produces an error diagnostic; the
  model still resolves for every other statement (partial-failure tolerance, matching flowchart's
  "drop the bad entry, keep going" discipline).
- [ ] Every declared participant resolves with `origin: "declared"` and a full-height lifeline
  extent (no `create`/`destroy` statements exist yet at this ticket's parser support level, so
  this is the only case to cover here — tickets 07/12 add the truncated-extent cases once
  create/destroy parsing exists).
- [ ] `title` and `autonumberOn`/`autonumberOff` statements pass through into the resolved
  `SequenceModel` unchanged (no validation needed on them).

## Test seam

`buildSequenceModel(document: SequenceDocument): { model: SequenceModel | null; diagnostics:
Diagnostic[] }` — unit level, pure function, hand-built `SequenceDocument` fixtures (does not
require ticket 01's real parser to exist first, only its frozen `contracts.ts` types).
